questions.text: Why must a rebuild comparison inspect referenced constants even when masked function bytes and relocation shapes match?

options.A: Identical instruction bytes can load different values from the referenced tables.
options.B: Masking relocation fields guarantees all referenced data is identical.
options.C: A matching relocation shape proves the candidate has the original source text.
options.D: Constant tables affect compiler speed but cannot affect function results.

questions.explanation: Matching instructions and relocation shapes can still point at different table contents. The wrong case10 candidate matches the code but changes the final table entry from 4 to 3.

questions.text: A rebuild passes ten ordinary test cases but widens a 32-bit multiply to long. Which additional test class best targets this change?

options.A: Inputs that exercise only the zero-divisor guard.
options.B: Inputs that preserve small positive intermediate values.
options.C: Inputs that make the original intermediate overflow 32 bits.
options.D: Inputs that repeat the same ordinary cases in a new order.

questions.explanation: Widening changes when the product wraps. Overflow cells distinguish the original fixed-width compiled behavior from the wide rebuild; the oracle architecture and build must be recorded.

questions.text: aggregate returns fail if any status is fail; otherwise it returns unknown for an empty list or any non-pass status, and pass otherwise. What does aggregate(["pass", "unknown", "fail"]) return?
questions.explanation: The fail check runs first, so any fail wins even when unknown is also present.
